<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451, which in positive mode corresponds to [M + H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈182.0378 Da. The formula C₁₂H₆O₂ matches this mass (calculated monoisotopic mass = 182.0368 Da, within a few ppm) and reproduces the observed M+1 (≈10 % intensity) pattern expected from 12 carbons. No other common heteroatoms are required. Therefore the molecular formula is C12H6O2.</thought>
<final_answer>C12H6O2</final_answer>
